title: Mortgage Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Mortgage Calculator: Estimate your monthly home loan payment and lifetime interest. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers…
content:
The [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate your monthly home loan payment and lifetime interest. Enter your loan amount, interest rate (yearly) and term and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A mortgage calculator estimates the principal-and-interest payment on a home loan. It's the starting point for working out how much house you can afford. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) and [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator). People also look for this tool as "home loan calculator", "mortgage payment calculator", "house payment calculator".

## How to use the Mortgage Calculator

Start by entering your loan amount, then entering your interest rate (yearly) (%) and finally entering your term (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your loan amount.
2. Enter your interest rate (yearly) (%).
3. Enter your term (years).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 350,000 mortgage at 6.5% over 30 years costs about 2,212.24 per month, and roughly 446,406 in interest over the full term. Try the same figures in the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Loan amount: 350000, Interest rate (yearly): 6.5 %, Term: 30 years), the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) returns Monthly payment: 2,212.24, Total interest: 446,405.71, Total repaid: 796,405.71, Number of payments: 360. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Add property tax, insurance and HOA fees for your true monthly cost.
- A 15-year term typically has a lower rate and far less interest.
- A larger down payment can remove private mortgage insurance (PMI).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does this include taxes and insurance?

No — it shows principal and interest only. Add property tax, homeowner's insurance and any PMI to get your full housing payment. Try it with your own numbers in the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How much house can I afford?

A common guideline is to keep total housing costs below about 28% of gross monthly income. Try it with your own numbers in the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Mortgage Calculator use?

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments. You can see it in action in the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Mortgage Calculator?

Just Loan amount, Interest rate (yearly) and Term. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### Is the Mortgage Calculator free to use?

Yes. The Mortgage Calculator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and start straight away.
